close.note: Follow-up to scoped-integrity-preflight. Diagnoses recoverable scopes; does not reconstruct sprint.json. CHANGELOG entry sits under Unreleased; no release decision taken.
close.summary: Scope identity derived from evidence, with the contamination repair path it required.
recommendations: Move the Unreleased entry into a version before publishing; 4.47.1 is already on npm.
Consider promoting the evidence-over-path rule to a global convention with kyro rule add --global.
Next line: honest provenance for maker/checker and approvals, then startup consolidation.
learnings: The first plan proposed a rule (no sprint.json means not a scope) that would have hidden the very case recover mode exists to rescue; the counter-rule matters as much as the rule.
A narrowing rule needs its own repair path: unregister-orphan refused whenever the path existed, which would have made the new classification a dead end for anyone already contaminated.
A test asserted the defect as expected behaviour (an empty folder registering as a planning scope), so the suite was green while the bug was live.

beforeClose.title: Scope identity from evidence, not from a directory existing
beforeClose.objective: Stop an arbitrary directory under scopes/ from becoming a scope, without hiding a scope that lost its sprint.json but can still be recovered.
successCriteria: A directory with no Kyro artifacts never blocks integrity, never resolves as a scope, and is never registered.
A scope that lost sprint.json but keeps a usable close checkpoint stays visible and is reported as recoverable.
Kyro artifacts without a usable recovery path are reported as damaged without promising a resume.
A registry entry pointing at a foreign directory can be cleaned without touching a byte of that directory.
An explicit --kyro-scope naming a foreign directory fails as a wrong name, not as a damaged scope.

requirements.statement: Directory classification must be derived from evidence on disk and crossed with registry membership, not inferred from the directory existing.
requirements.rationale: Treating every directory as a scope made a stray folder a hard integrity blocker across the whole project.

requirements.statement: A directory holding no recognizable Kyro artifacts must be ignored by discovery, resolution and integrity, and surfaced only as non-blocking advice.
requirements.rationale: Silence would leave the user unable to learn why their folder never appears as a scope.

requirements.statement: A scope that lost sprint.json but retains at least one usable close checkpoint must remain discoverable and be reported as recoverable.
requirements.rationale: Refusing to call it a scope would hide exactly the case recover mode exists to rescue.

requirements.statement: Kyro artifacts without a usable close checkpoint must be reported as damaged, never as recoverable.
requirements.rationale: A remediation record or a corrupt checkpoint is evidence of ownership, not a recovery path; promising a resume that cannot happen is worse than reporting damage.

requirements.statement: Only directories Kyro can describe truthfully may be written into the project registry.
requirements.rationale: Rehydrate invented a planning status for unreadable directories, turning a filesystem accident into persisted project state.

requirements.statement: A registry entry whose directory is foreign must be cleanable, removing only the entry and preserving the directory byte for byte.
requirements.rationale: Unregister refused whenever the path existed, so installs already contaminated by an earlier rehydrate had no repair path at all.

requirements.statement: An explicit scope argument naming a foreign directory must fail as a missing scope on every entry point that accepts one.
requirements.rationale: An explicit flag must not be a way around discovery, and a wrong name is not an integrity problem.

requirements.statement: A registered scope whose sprint.json is invalid must classify as corrupt.
requirements.rationale: Identity derivation returned null and nothing checked, so a corrupt registered scope was reported as healthy.

scenarios.given: a directory under scopes/ holding only unrelated files
scenarios.when: integrity prepare, scope list and doctor run
scenarios.then: nothing blocks, the directory is absent from the scope list, and only a global doctor reports it as a warning

scenarios.given: a workspace containing a foreign directory under scopes/
scenarios.when: install or sync rehydrates the registry
scenarios.then: project.json does not contain an entry for it

scenarios.given: a scope whose sprint.json was removed but whose archive keeps a checkpoint naming that scope
scenarios.then: it is reported as recoverable-no-sprint and remains visible to doctor --artifacts

scenarios.given: a directory with Kyro artifacts whose only checkpoint is unreadable
scenarios.then: it is reported as owned-damaged and never as recoverable

scenarios.given: a registry entry written by an earlier rehydrate whose directory is foreign
scenarios.then: the entry is removed and the directory is byte-identical afterwards

scenarios.given: an explicit scope argument naming a foreign directory
scenarios.when: status, context-pack, integrity prepare or doctor --artifacts run
scenarios.then: each fails with SCOPE_NOT_FOUND rather than an integrity classification

scenarios.given: a leftover directory containing only a legacy trace folder
scenarios.when: scope discovery runs after the special case is deleted
scenarios.then: it is still never treated as a scope

scenarios.given: a scope registered in project.json whose sprint.json is invalid
scenarios.then: it classifies as corrupt rather than present-and-registered

nonGoals: Reconstructing sprint.json from a checkpoint after-image; this scope diagnoses, it does not repair.
Adding states to the scope entry status vocabulary, which would force a schema migration.
Changing the 4.47.1 release or its scopes.
Provenance for maker/checker approvals, tracked separately.

conventions.rule: Identity comes from evidence on disk, never from a path existing. A namespace directory anyone can create must not confer meaning.
Finding artifacts proves ownership, not recoverability. Never report a repair path the tool cannot actually execute.
Any rule that narrows what the tool accepts must ship with the repair path for state the old rule already wrote.

roadmap.sizingRationale: One sprint: a single classification primitive plus the consumers that must respect it, all provable through the existing blast-radius gate.

activeSprint.title: Evidence-based scope classification
activeSprint.objective: Classify scope directories from evidence, make every consumer respect that classification, and make the resulting contamination cleanable.

phases.title: Classification primitives
phases.objective: Introduce a neutral checkpoint survey and an evidence-based directory classifier without inverting layers.

tasks.title: Add a neutral checkpoint discovery module
tasks.description: Add src/cli/checkpoints/discovery.ts returning structured facts about a scope's close checkpoints, built on resolveEffectiveCheckpointAtPath so a checkpoint only counts when it resolves and its identity names the scope.
tasks.context: The equivalent logic lived in commands/artifact-doctor.ts, which returns CheckResult[]; importing it from artifacts/ would invert the dependency and risk cycles. A third copy of the readdir/filter pattern also existed in integrity-plan.ts.
acceptance_criteria: The module returns structured data, not presentation types.
A checkpoint counts as usable only when it resolves to valid or canonicalized and its identity matches the scope.
No module under artifacts/ imports from commands/.
The duplicate checkpoint listing in integrity-plan.ts is removed.

evidence.summary: Added src/cli/checkpoints/discovery.ts returning structured checkpoint facts built on resolveEffectiveCheckpointAtPath, and removed the duplicate checkpoint listing from integrity-plan.ts.
validation: A checkpoint copied from another scope is correctly rejected as unusable (identity mismatch), proving presence alone is not the signal
artifacts/ imports checkpoints/, never commands/; verified src/cli/checkpoints does not import artifacts/scopes so no cycle exists
npm run typecheck and npm run build clean

checked_criteria: The module returns structured data, not presentation types.
A checkpoint counts as usable only when it resolves to valid or canonicalized and its identity matches the scope.
No module under artifacts/ imports from commands/.
The duplicate checkpoint listing in integrity-plan.ts is removed.

tasks.title: Classify scope directories from evidence
tasks.description: Add the five-way directory classifier and derive listOwnedScopeDirectories, listRegistrableScopeDirectories and listForeignScopeDirectories from it. Keep listScopeFolders as a compatibility wrapper. Extract readScopeSprint as the single sprint reader and remove the 4.47.1 trace-only special case.
tasks.context: listScopeFolders returned every directory under scopes/, feeding roughly ten consumers including registry writes.
acceptance_criteria: Directories classify as valid, corrupt, recoverable, owned-damaged or foreign.
An empty archive directory is not evidence of ownership.
The trace-only special case is deleted and its behaviour still holds through the general rule.
Sprint reading and validation exist in exactly one place.

evidence.summary: Added SCOPE_DIR_CLASS with the five-way classifier, derived listOwnedScopeDirectories / listRegistrableScopeDirectories / listForeignScopeDirectories from it, kept listScopeFolders as a compatibility wrapper, extracted readScopeSprint, and deleted the trace-only special case.
validation: Sandbox: notes-backup and .ds-junk classify FOREIGN; global prepare returns blockers: []
check:blast-radius-isolation still asserts a trace-only leftover is never a scope, now via the general rule
Falsification: replacing the owned-class filter with a pass-through makes the gate fail

checked_criteria: Directories classify as valid, corrupt, recoverable, owned-damaged or foreign.
An empty archive directory is not evidence of ownership.
The trace-only special case is deleted and its behaviour still holds through the general rule.
Sprint reading and validation exist in exactly one place.

phases.title: Consumers and repair
phases.objective: Make classification actually govern registry classification, integrity reporting, registry writes and explicit scope arguments.

tasks.title: Derive registry classification from both axes
tasks.description: Classify from the cross product of directory class and registry membership: distinguish recoverable, owned-damaged and corrupt instead of one bucket, treat a registered foreign directory as an orphan, and stop reporting a registered scope with an invalid sprint.json as healthy.
tasks.context: classifyOne collapsed missing, invalid and not-a-scope into IRRECONCILABLE, and a registered scope with an invalid sprint fell through to present-and-registered.
acceptance_criteria: Recoverable, owned-damaged and corrupt are distinct classifications.
A registered id whose directory is foreign classifies as a registered orphan.
A registered scope with an invalid sprint.json classifies as corrupt.
A directory that is absent still classifies as it did before.

evidence.summary: classifyOne now derives from directory class crossed with registry membership: recoverable, owned-damaged and corrupt are distinct; a registered id whose directory is foreign becomes a registered orphan; a registered scope with an invalid sprint.json is no longer reported as healthy.
validation: Sandbox: registered entry + foreign directory produces targets.unregister, not a blocker
Sandbox: demo without sprint.json but with its own checkpoint classifies recoverable, not irreconcilable
check:scope-remediation 716 assertions and check:repair-integrity 90 assertions still pass

checked_criteria: Recoverable, owned-damaged and corrupt are distinct classifications.
A registered id whose directory is foreign classifies as a registered orphan.
A registered scope with an invalid sprint.json classifies as corrupt.
A directory that is absent still classifies as it did before.

tasks.title: Report recoverable and damaged as different blockers
tasks.description: Add distinct integrity blocker codes so a scope with a usable checkpoint points at the resume path while Kyro artifacts without one are reported as damaged with no promise of recovery.
tasks.context: Both cases previously produced the same irreconcilable blocker, giving the operator no signal about which one could actually come back.
acceptance_criteria: recoverable-no-sprint names how many usable checkpoints exist.
owned-damaged states that no automatic recovery path exists.
Corrupt sprint.json keeps the irreconcilable code.

evidence.summary: Added recoverable-no-sprint and owned-damaged blocker codes with distinct messages; corrupt sprint.json keeps irreconcilable.
validation: Sandbox: recoverable-no-sprint reports '1 usable close checkpoint(s) in archive/ can resume it'
Sandbox: a directory whose only checkpoint is unreadable reports owned-damaged and never claims recoverability

checked_criteria: recoverable-no-sprint names how many usable checkpoints exist.
owned-damaged states that no automatic recovery path exists.
Corrupt sprint.json keeps the irreconcilable code.

tasks.title: Make contaminated registry entries cleanable
tasks.description: Change unregister-orphan so it re-verifies the directory is still foreign at apply time, aborts if Kyro evidence appeared, removes only the registry entry, and never modifies the directory.
tasks.context: applyUnregister threw DIVERGED whenever the directory existed, so an entry an earlier rehydrate wrote for a stray folder could never be removed.
acceptance_criteria: A registered foreign directory can be unregistered.
The directory is preserved byte for byte.
Evidence appearing between prepare and apply still aborts with DIVERGED.

evidence.summary: applyUnregister re-classifies at apply time and proceeds only when the directory is absent or still foreign, removing just the registry entry.
validation: Sandbox: contaminated entry cleaned; README.md SHA-256 identical before and after; directory still present
Falsification: restoring the old existsSync guard makes the gate fail with 'Scope directory notes-backup reappeared before apply'

checked_criteria: A registered foreign directory can be unregistered.
The directory is preserved byte for byte.
Evidence appearing between prepare and apply still aborts with DIVERGED.

tasks.title: Restrict registry writes and explicit scope arguments
tasks.description: Point rehydrate and the install prompt at registrable directories only, remove the fabricated planning fallback, and reject an explicit scope naming a foreign directory across resolution, integrity prepare and artifact doctor.
tasks.context: rehydrate minted a planning entry for any unreadable directory, and an explicit --kyro-scope bypassed discovery entirely.
acceptance_criteria: Only valid scopes are registered by install and sync.
The install prompt lists only what will actually be registered.
An explicit foreign scope fails SCOPE_NOT_FOUND on status, context-pack, integrity prepare and artifact doctor.

evidence.summary: rehydrate and the install prompt now use listRegistrableScopeDirectories, the fabricated planning fallback is gone, and assertNotForeignDirectory guards resolution, integrity prepare and artifact doctor.
validation: Sandbox: status, context-pack, repair integrity prepare and doctor --artifacts with --kyro-scope notes-backup all exit non-zero with SCOPE_NOT_FOUND
check:install-rehydrate updated and passing: a foreign directory is no longer registered

checked_criteria: Only valid scopes are registered by install and sync.
The install prompt lists only what will actually be registered.
An explicit foreign scope fails SCOPE_NOT_FOUND on status, context-pack, integrity prepare and artifact doctor.

phases.title: Advisory, gate and documentation
phases.objective: Keep ignored directories visible without blocking, prove the whole contract, and record the behaviour change.

tasks.title: Warn about ignored directories on global doctor only
tasks.description: Add a non-blocking doctor check listing directories under scopes/ that are not Kyro scopes, emitted only when no scope is requested.
tasks.context: Ignoring foreign directories silently would leave a user with no way to learn why their folder never appears as a scope.
acceptance_criteria: The check warns and never fails.
A scoped doctor does not emit it.

evidence.summary: Added checkForeignScopeDirectories, a WARN-only doctor check emitted solely when no scope is requested.
validation: Sandbox: global doctor prints '[WARN] scope directories: 2 ... ignored: .ds-junk, notes-backup' and exits 0
Sandbox: doctor --kyro-scope demo does not emit the warning

checked_criteria: The check warns and never fails.
A scoped doctor does not emit it.

tasks.title: Extend the blast-radius gate to the full matrix
tasks.description: Add regressions for foreign directories, recoverable versus damaged, pre-existing contamination with byte preservation, and explicit foreign scope arguments, rather than adding another bespoke check script.
tasks.context: check-install-rehydrate asserted that a directory with no sprint.json registers with a planning status, encoding the defect as expected behaviour.
acceptance_criteria: The matrix of directory class and registry membership is covered.
The rehydrate test asserts a foreign directory is not registered.
Reverting either the discovery filter or the unregister fix makes the gate fail.
No new check script is added.

evidence.summary: Extended check:blast-radius-isolation with foreign-directory, recoverable-vs-damaged, pre-existing-contamination and explicit-foreign-scope regressions, and rewrote the check-install-rehydrate assertion that encoded the defect. No new check script was added.
validation: Falsification 1: pass-through discovery filter makes the gate fail
Falsification 2: restoring the old unregister guard makes the gate fail
Contamination case asserts SHA-256 equality of the foreign file before and after apply
npm run check passes end to end, exit 0

checked_criteria: The matrix of directory class and registry membership is covered.
The rehydrate test asserts a foreign directory is not registered.
Reverting either the discovery filter or the unregister fix makes the gate fail.
No new check script is added.

tasks.title: Document the behaviour change
tasks.description: Record the change under Unreleased and correct the docs that describe rehydration and doctor warnings, without deciding a release version.
tasks.context: 4.47.1 is already published and this is a separate behavioural change.
acceptance_criteria: The change is described under Unreleased.
Rehydration and doctor documentation match the new behaviour.
No version field changes.

evidence.summary: Recorded the behaviour change under CHANGELOG Unreleased and corrected docs/teams.md rehydration wording and docs/cli.md doctor warning list. No version field touched.
validation: check:versions still reports all versions matching 4.47.1
check:links passes over the edited docs

checked_criteria: The change is described under Unreleased.
Rehydration and doctor documentation match the new behaviour.
No version field changes.

definitionOfDone: A directory with no Kyro artifacts never blocks integrity, never resolves, and is never registered.
A scope with a usable close checkpoint but no sprint.json stays discoverable and is reported as recoverable.
Kyro artifacts without a usable checkpoint are reported as damaged with no promise of recovery.
A registry entry pointing at a foreign directory is cleanable with the directory preserved byte for byte.
An explicit foreign scope fails SCOPE_NOT_FOUND on every entry point that accepts one.
The blast-radius gate covers the matrix and fails when either fix is reverted.
npm run check passes end to end and the real workspace stays green.
